certification: CodeForge ForgeGreen Phase 3 (FG-8) sustainability & resource measurement — FG-8R live-measurement closure

revisionHistory.summary: Initial measurement infrastructure: receipt schema, normalization boundary, waste taxonomy, baseline framework, pluggable energy estimator, hardware-telemetry interface, cross-receipt integrity logic, append-only persistence, lifecycle events, 7 synthetic benchmark fixtures. Two gaps explicitly acknowledged and left open: (1) RouteReceipt/FinancialReceipt not wired into the live integration point, (2) Baseline B had no automatic live context-population source.

Closure phase. This artifact reflects FG-8R's reconciled, corrected state and supersedes the FG-8 revision above as the current certification authority. See `reconciliation` below for exactly what the FG-8 narrative got wrong and what this revision corrected.

architecture.decision: FG-8 (and this FG-8R closure) extends the existing certified ForgeGreen subsystem (packages/forge-green, FG-1 through FG-7) rather than creating a colliding or parallel subsystem under the same name — a user-directed decision made during FG-8 and unchanged here.
architecture.fg8rKeyFinding: The FG-8R task assumed `RouteReceipt`/`FinancialReceipt` (packages/eight-bit/src/receipts.ts) were a real live authority not yet wired to FG-8. Direct investigation found this is NOT accurate: `createRouteReceipt`/`createFinancialReceipt` are called nowhere in the entire repository outside their own definition file — not in production code, not in eight-bit's own tests. The REAL live authority the production routing path actually constructs and persists is a `DecisionReceipt` (packages/eight-bit/src/types.ts), written by `EightBitDecisionStore.recordReceipt` on a rotation/failover event, plus the `FreeModelRecord` ForgeZero/the firewall verifies for whichever model actually executed (read via `firewall.getModel(provider, model)`, using `AgentUsage.provider`/`.model` — the real post-hoc dispatch, not the a-priori `req.modelSelection`, which the investigation found is undefined in the vast majority of live sub-agent runs). FG-8R wires the SustainabilityReceipt's cross-receipt integrity layer to this REAL live authority instead of the unused schema, per the task's own instruction to 'use the real existing lifecycle' and 'not invent another parallel receipt authority'. The RouteReceipt/FinancialReceipt-shaped inputs remain supported (fully tested) for forward compatibility, should 8-Bit ever construct them live.

genuineBugFoundAndFixedDuringFg8r.bug: Receipt id (`SustainabilityReceipt.receiptId`) was hashed from identity + a normalization-version string only, never from the actual measured content. Two genuinely DIFFERENT measurements for the same run/session identity (e.g. a retry that legitimately observed MORE work) collided on the same receiptId, so the append-only `insertIfAbsent` store would silently DROP the second, more-complete measurement.
genuineBugFoundAndFixedDuringFg8r.foundBy: fg8r-duplicate-finalization-retry.test.ts's second test case (required by task §12), which failed on first run.
genuineBugFoundAndFixedDuringFg8r.fix: `identityFingerprint` in packages/forge-green/src/sustainability-receipt.ts now hashes the full measured content (tokens/tools/verification/routing/context/timing/crossReceiptIntegrity/wasteBreakdown/baselines-minus-timestamps/energy/carbon) in addition to identity — content-addressed, matching the FG-1D canonical-cache philosophy already used elsewhere in this codebase. An exact retry of identical measured content still yields the identical id (true idempotency); a retry that legitimately observed different content now yields a genuinely different id (never silently merged).

genuineBugFoundAndFixedDuringFg8r.bug: `simulateBaselineB` did not reject a negative `actualTransmittedBytes`, so malformed/impossible population input (e.g. -50 bytes transmitted) could pass its `> naivePolicyBytes` guard and produce a nonsensical >100%-savings comparison.
genuineBugFoundAndFixedDuringFg8r.fix: packages/forge-green/src/baseline.ts now rejects non-finite and negative `actualTransmittedBytes`/`naivePolicyBytes` before computing a comparison — returns `undefined` (no baseline claim) instead.

liveCrossReceiptWiring.flow: RouteReceipt/FinancialReceipt authority -> unused in production (verified). REAL flow: AgentRuntime.persistForgeGreenSustainabilityReceipt reads AgentUsage.provider/.model (the actual dispatched model, set from real provider responses) -> firewall.getModel(provider, model) returns the live FreeModelRecord ForgeZero verified (costProfile.isFree, accessClass, freeStatus) -> EightBitDecisionStore.listReceipts(sessionId) is queried and filtered to this runId for any persisted DecisionReceipt (rotation/failover) evidence -> both are passed into createSustainabilityReceipt({ live: { freeModelRecord, decisionReceipts } }) -> checkCrossReceiptIntegrity derives financialClassification/financialClassificationSource from the live record (never from a recomputation) and cross-checks the live model against the MOST RECENT DecisionReceipt's selected route, surfacing any disagreement as measurementStatus:'incomplete' with explicit reason codes rather than silently reconciling.
liveCrossReceiptWiring.commonCase: In a typical live run, `decisionReceipts` is EMPTY — a DecisionReceipt is written only on an actual rotation/failover event, not on every run. This is expected and does not degrade `financialClassification`, which is derived independently from the live FreeModelRecord.
liveCrossReceiptWiring.testEvidence: packages/forge-green/test/fg8r-live-cross-receipt.test.ts (7 tests), packages/forge-green/test/fg8r-live-lifecycle.test.ts (2 tests, full 12-stage lifecycle including this wiring end to end).

liveContextBaseline.flow: Baseline B's eligible population comes from RepositoryIntelligence.getCompleteness() (analyzableFiles vs skippedFiles — a single cheap already-existing query) plus ONE bounded RepositoryIntelligence.listFiles({ limit: cap }) call. QueryPage.truncated tells the adapter, without a second call, whether that single bounded page covered every eligible file: if not truncated, eligibleBytes/naivePolicyBytes are an EXACT sum over every returned file's real stored size (never a sample or extrapolation) plus a real binary/generated/sensitive breakdown; if truncated (workspace larger than the bounded cap), bytes are explicitly reported unavailable rather than computed from an undercounted partial page — never fake precision. Actual-transmitted bytes/tokens come from AgentContextMetrics.contextBytes/.estimatedInputTokens, hoisted into module-scope variables in agent-runtime.ts to survive across the function's try/finally boundary safely.

preExistingFailures.cause: better-sqlite3@12.11.1's prebuild-install places its compiled addon at node_modules/better-sqlite3/bin/win32-x64-130/better-sqlite3.node; the classic `bindings` package (which better-sqlite3's own lib/database.js calls as `require('bindings')('better_sqlite3.node')`) only searches legacy paths (build/Release/better_sqlite3.node and similar) and never finds it. This is a packaging/install-path mismatch between better-sqlite3's own install script and the `bindings` package's search list — not a Node ABI mismatch (both reference ABI 130) and not related to any FG-8/FG-8R file.
preExistingFailures.whyItDoesNotAffectFg8OrFg8r: packages/sessions/src/sqlite.ts prefers Node's built-in `node:sqlite` (available in this environment, Node v24.19.0) and only falls back to better-sqlite3 when node:sqlite is unavailable (documented reason: the Electron desktop runtime currently bundles Node 20.x, which lacks node:sqlite). Every FG-8/FG-8R test that uses `createSessionPersistence` — including all restart/rehydration/duplicate-finalization tests — uses the default (node:sqlite) driver and never touches this code path. Only the ONE test that explicitly forces `driver: 'better-sqlite3'` to test that alternate backend in isolation is affected.
preExistingFailures.investigationMethod: Non-destructive: inspected node_modules/better-sqlite3's actual installed file layout, its package.json install script, its lib/database.js source, and packages/sessions/src/sqlite.ts's driver-selection logic directly. No git stash, no dependency reinstall, no repository state was touched to confirm this.
preExistingFailures.classification: pre-existing, environmental (local dependency-installation packaging quirk), confirmed NOT caused or exposed by FG-8/FG-8R
